subject: Offsite erasure lag — windows, restore boundaries, and procurement evidence
messages:
From: Daniel Morris <daniel@fintech-partner.com>

Cc: LegalTeam <legal@fintech-partner.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on offsite erase windows and restore impact

Hi Hannah,

Quick question from our security and procurement teams as we finalize the contract: we need a clear explanation of how offsite snapshot deletion (expire/expunge) propagates across regions and the practical impact on restore windows. Specifically:

- If a snapshot is scheduled to expire at T (customer-requested deletion or TTL-based), what is the expected range of time before that data is irreversibly expunged in another region (replica)?
- Does the system keep tombstone metadata that would allow a point-in-time restore after the primary is purged? If so, for how long?
- Are there circumstances where data could be restored from an older replica after the primary delete — and if so, how long are those replicas retained before expunge?

We received the snapshot-manifest-20270421.csv (attached) and want to map the retention/erase behavior for those snapshots. Procurement also needs a short note we can pass to procurement/legal about guaranteed boundaries and typical propagation lag for SLA language.

Thanks — can you loop in engineering if deeper detail is required?

—Daniel
Head of Infrastructure, Fintech Partner

Attachments: snapshot-manifest-20270421.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then I’ll pull engineering into specifics and provide a one-page procurement-friendly note.

Highlights:
- Typical expunge propagation: 6–48 hours depending on region replication backlog and ongoing maintenance. Most common is 6–24 hours under normal conditions.
- Tombstones/metadata: we retain tombstone markers and snapshot metadata after a logical delete for an additional configurable hold period (default 7 days) to support manual recovery and compliance holds.
- Cross-region restore: If replicas have not yet been expunged, restores from the replica are possible; once expunge completes, that data is irrecoverable.

I’m looping in Rishi with a quick request: can you add the precise expunge SLAs we can commit to (best-effort vs contractual) and note any conditions that extend the window (scheduled maintenance, region outage, manual retention overrides)? Also attaching our internal restore playbook for reference.

We’ll produce: (a) a short two-paragraph procurement note summarizing guaranteed vs typical windows, and (b) the deeper timeline matrix showing normal/peak/incident ranges.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on offsite erase windows and restore impact

Daniel / Hannah —

Adding technical detail (summary, then specifics):

Summary: expunge is an eventually consistent operation across replicas. Typical end-to-end window is 6–24 hours, but in operational incidents (region failover, large backlog, or cross-region throttling) it can extend to 48–72 hours in extreme cases. We do not rely on replicas as a long-term "backup after delete"; once the expunge workflow completes on all replicas, restoration is not possible.

Details:
- Stages: logical-delete -> tombstone creation -> background sweep/compaction -> expunge-on-replica (async).
- Tombstone metadata: retained by default for 7 days (configurable per-customer for Private deployments). During that retention the metadata supports automated and manual restore operations (metadata includes snapshot manifest and object index).
- Replica behavior: replicas apply tombstone markers on receipt; replicas with delayed apply due to backlog will still honor tombstone upon processing, which is why you might see a narrow window where data is present on a far replica for a short time after primary deletion. That window is not a durability guarantee.
- Legal/hold: we support retention holds that override automatic expunge; if a hold is placed, expunge is suspended until hold removal. This is the recommended path for legal preservation.

Operational recommendations for Fintech Partner:
1) If you require a contractual expunge boundary, we can set a max expunge SLA of 72 hours in the contract with explicit incident carve-outs (maintenance, force majeure).
2) For high-assurance restores beyond default tombstone retention, enable snapshot archiving (export to your S3 bucket) or increase tombstone retention for your private/dedicated deployment.
3) For procurement evidence, use the attached expunge-timeline-diagram.svg and our standard restore playbook; we can produce a short attestation describing normal vs guaranteed windows.

I’ve attached a diagram showing the pipeline and typical timing. Happy to walk through with your ops team.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
